restructure_mandate.why: Owner review 2026-08-14 found the portfolio had become a closet index fund: 17 positions of which 6 were ETFs (SCHD/XLI/XLV are subsets of VOO; XLV also duplicates the LLY holding), the 11 single names are all large-cap S&P constituents VOO already holds, and ~39% of the account (14.0% idle cash + ~$253 of duplicate ETFs) expressed no research view at all. Result: +2.81% vs SPY +2.89% — tracking the index and losing to it slightly. Owner chose a moderately aggressive, research-driven strategy instead. Read the rewritten STRATEGY.md in full before acting.
steps: 1. SELL IN FULL: SCHD, XLI, XLV — pure VOO duplicates (~$150 combined). Not optional.

2. DECIDE VXUS and IJR — your call, no default lean. They are the only non-US-large-cap exposure; dropping both leaves the book a single US mega-cap macro bet, which cuts against the 'not too aggressive' mandate. Keeping them as a small satellite sleeve OR redeploying into researched names are both legitimate — justify whichever you pick in writing.

3. RE-UNDERWRITE all 11 single names (VOO NVDA MSFT AMZN GOOGL JPM LLY XOM COST NEE LIN PLD). Apply the beat-the-index test to each: write a specific why_not_voo line. Rank by conviction and EXIT THE WEAKEST down to 8-10 names. Explicitly assess the NVDA/MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL cluster against the new ~40% correlated-theme cap — four names, four sector labels, one AI/cloud bet.
4. TOP UP VOO to a 15-20% core (~$180) this cycle.

5. STAGE THE SINGLE-NAME BUYS ACROSS CYCLES 13 AND 14 — do not deploy all proceeds at one moment's prices. Turnover cost is trivial (<$1 total, commission-free, liquid names at ~0.01-0.05% spreads), so staging is nearly free protection against one bad entry point.
6. TARGET END STATE after Cycle 14: 9-11 total positions, each single name ~$90-110 (~9-11%), VOO 15-20%, cash 2-5%, >=4 sectors, no sector >35%, no correlated theme >40%.
7. Populate why_not_voo and theme on EVERY surviving holding, and seed benchmark_history each cycle going forward.
8. If the market is closed when Cycle 13 fires, do the full analysis and defer all orders to the next open-market cycle (existing rule).
9. When the target end state is reached, set this block's status to DONE with the completing cycle number — do not delete it (it is the record of why the portfolio changed shape).

lessons: cycles 1-7 (retrospective, added with the strategy upgrade): The CAT round-trip validated evidence-based decisions both ways - cycle 5 correctly held CAT through a -5% dip when research showed strength (dividend raise, target hikes), and cycle 7 correctly exited when research showed real deterioration (margin compression, tariff guide, downgrade). The differentiator was actual research, not the price move itself.

Distinguishing 'guidance landed a hair below consensus on a premium multiple' from 'the business is actually deteriorating' is exactly the kind of judgment call this process exists to make well.

cycle 9: MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL continued rallying into Friday's close after the Cycle 8 mid-session beat check — a real earnings beat tends to keep compounding through the session and beyond, reinforcing that holding through the print (not trimming into strength out of nervousness) was the right call.

cycle 10: CAT beat Q2 estimates by 32% with a record $72B backlog — the Cycle 7 exit thesis reversed faster than expected. Lesson: a cyclical's margin narrative can flip in one quarter given a real demand catalyst, but a same-day +5-11% earnings pop is still a chase, not an entry — wait for the move to settle before acting on a reversed thesis.

cycle 10: LIN's fundamentals stayed healthy but the stock was in a confirmed technical downtrend — a reminder that 'the business is fine' and 'the chart says wait' can both be true at once; STRATEGY.md's scoring rubric (trend scored 1/5) did its job by blocking an add into a falling knife despite good fundamentals.

cycle 11: CAT's post-earnings spike fully round-tripped within 3 trading days — confirms the execution rule against chasing >5% intraday pops: even a real fundamental reversal needs the move to consolidate, not just fade, before it's a legitimate technical entry.

The cause was a self-contradicting brief: 'maximize long-term profit' paired with rules (15-20 names, >=6 sectors, always hold an ETF core, 5-15% cash) that mandate becoming the index. Lesson: diversification rules and a profit-maximizing mandate pull in opposite directions, and when they conflict the rules win silently. Every dollar must express a view — hence the new why_not_voo test on every holding.

cycles 10-12 (owner review 2026-08-14): The four-cycle no-trade stretch was misdiagnosed as an over-strict scoring bar. It was not — the no-trade calls were individually defensible (CAT's spike really did round-trip). The actual failure was a FUNNEL of only three stale candidates (LIN/AMT/CAT) re-checked cycle after cycle, with zero new names screened and no scanners ever built. Lesson: when nothing passes the bar, screen more candidates; never lower the bar. That is doubly true now that the book is concentrated and each position carries more weight.
